claims.text: As-synthesized (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 has relatively coarse, continuous grain boundaries.
The coarse, continuous grain-boundary structure contributes to crack susceptibility in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
A crystallographic domain distribution in the alloy is responsible for its caloric response.
A tailored annealing treatment followed by controlled cooling can produce a bimodal grain structure in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38.
The resulting bimodal structure will contain fine grain networks interspersed with larger grains.
Fine grain networks will enhance ductility and resistance to crack propagation.
Retained larger grains will remain calorically active and preserve the crystallographic phases needed for the caloric effect.
The proposed thermal treatment will promote recrystallization and controlled grain growth.
Processing-temperature changes can alter grain size and phase content in a high-entropy alloy.
The treated alloy will have significantly greater load-bearing integrity than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit reduced cracking and enhanced fracture toughness relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy's caloric response under magnetic fields will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy's caloric response under pressure fields will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy has a large caloric effect but poor load-bearing integrity and a tendency to crack.
Departures from the suitable annealing temperature or cooling rate may alter the caloric-active phases.
The intervention is applicable within the temperature, magnetic-field, pressure-field, and mechanical-loading ranges typical of caloric refrigeration devices.
